stage_a.note: Confident, engaged delivery with a positive, professional tone throughout the presentation.
Shows animated engagement and excitement when explaining the product's motivational effect.
Polite and approachable demeanor, though primarily focused on delivering the pitch material matter-of-factly.

venture.description: Sweat-activated technology applied to apparel that reveals a hidden design or message when the fabric gets wet.
venture.note: The founder currently sells decorated shirts but intends to license the technology to major apparel brands.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder pitches ViewSport, sweat-activated technology for apparel that reveals hidden designs during workouts, seeking investment to grow.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks for the current sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states they have done one hundred forty thousand dollars this year, mostly in the last three months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks to see one of the shirts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder hands a sample shirt to the panel.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor asks if the technology is invented by the founder or licensed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms he invented the technology and holds a pending patent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks about the founder's background and how he invented it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains his chemistry background and how observing sweat patterns while in medical school inspired the idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if the founder quit medical school.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms he did.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if he is pursuing this business full time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms he is working on it full time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor questions whether the gimmick would actually motivate a purchase.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder clarifies the value is in the technology as a new medium for branding, not just the shirt itself.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks if the strategy is to license the technology to apparel companies.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms the plan is to license to apparel and other textile manufacturers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if the current sales revenue comes from licensing deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains current sales are from their own decoration services applying the chemical to other brands' shirts.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks if sweating is required to see the hidden imprint.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder clarifies that any moisture works, giving the example of kids getting wet at water parks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor confirms that the fabric must be wet to reveal the design.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder agrees the fabric must be wet.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if the business model works by simply supplying the chemical.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms that licensing the chemical is the ultimate goal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if any companies have been approached for a licensing deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states that Hurley is currently very interested in the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks how intensely a person needs to work out to sweat enough to reveal the design.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states a twenty-minute workout by an average individual will produce the desired results.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if the revealed logo fades quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder admits that spraying from the outside is less effective than sweating from the inside.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder sprays water on a blue shirt to demonstrate the technology.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor notes that the design is not clearly visible on the sprayed shirt.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor asks if customers have complained about the design not being evident.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder denies ever receiving such complaints.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor remarks that the product demonstration is failing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor jokes that the founder is slipping up in his presentation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder shows a different grey shirt to demonstrate a clearer result.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor acknowledges that the text on the grey shirt is readable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks to look more closely at the grey shirt.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks if the material is cotton and if it works on pure cotton.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states the sample is polyester but the technology works on cotton.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks if the secondary black text can stand out as much as the primary text.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains the current designs are monochromatic but he is developing colors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks how the requested half a million dollars will be used.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains funds will drive awareness, secure partnerships with major brands, and build a sales team.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor challenges the valuation, noting they are paying for awareness that does not yet exist.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder defends the valuation by projecting half a million dollars in sales by the end of the year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor counters that if projections are met, the founder would not need their money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states he needs the investors' relationships.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor complains that he would be working for his own money after investing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder insists the technology has inherent value that justifies the investment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor exits, citing the incorrect strategy and excessive valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder announces a new purchase order from the US Naval Academy for three thousand shirts.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks to confirm the order quantity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms the quantity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks the founder to calculate the required earnings to justify a two and a half million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder guesses five hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor confirms and asks for current earnings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder repeats the current sales figure of one hundred forty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor points out the massive discrepancy between current earnings and the implied valuation multiple.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder reiterates he is looking for a partner to help grow a great technology.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor exits, stating the founder strategized incorrectly and asked for too much money.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor expresses insult at the valuation and questions why he should invest with no guaranteed return.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder attempts to justify the valuation by citing the massive size of the apparel industry.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor dismisses the industry size argument as a common and ineffective defense.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder points out that even major players have small market shares in the fragmented industry.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor exits, expressing frustration and taking financial offense at the arrogant valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor exits, criticizing the monochromatic design, the sweat requirement, and calling the product terrible.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor exits, stating he is not sold on the product and finds it gimmicky.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder thanks the panel for their time before leaving.

decisions.note: Feels he would be paying for awareness and working for his own money due to the high valuation.
States the founder strategized incorrectly and asked for too much money.
Expresses frustration with the strategic mistake and takes financial offense at the arrogant valuation.
Criticizes the monochromatic design, the sweat requirement, and calls the product terrible.
Is not sold on the product and finds it a bit gimmicky.
